memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Jacob heard that Laban's sons were saying, 'Jacob has taken everything our father owned and has gained all this wealth from what belonged to our father.' And Jacob noticed that Laban's attitude toward him was not what it had been. Then the LORD said to Jacob, 'Go back to the land of your fathers and to your relatives, and I will be with you.'" - Gen 31:1-3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The atmosphere in Laban's household has soured. Laban's sons are grumbling with jealousy, and Jacob senses that Laban himself no longer looks on him with favour. The warmth is gone; the season has changed. And right at that moment, God speaks: "Go back to the land of your fathers... and I will be with you."

Notice how God's timing works. For twenty years Jacob had stayed put, but now — just as the situation turns uncomfortable — God gives the word to move. Sometimes God uses a change in circumstances, even an unpleasant one, to nudge us toward the next step He has for us. The discomfort of a closing door can be part of His guidance.

Notice too the heart of God's promise: "I will be with you." Jacob was being sent back toward Esau, the brother who had once wanted to kill him. It would take courage. But God did not send him alone. The command to go came wrapped in the promise of His presence.

When God calls us to a new and uncertain step, He gives the same assurance. He never sends His children out empty-handed; He goes with them. If you sense a season ending and a new step ahead, listen for God's leading — and hold tightly to His promise, "I am with you."

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is God using a change in circumstances to nudge me toward a new step?
2. Where do I need to hear God's promise, "I will be with you"?
3. Am I willing to move when God says move, even toward the uncertain?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, help me to recognise Your leading when a season ends. Give me courage to take the step You call me to, holding tightly to Your promise to be with me. Amen.
